text:
Anya: heads up — eu-west-1 spot churn just spiked, +15% Pi-day interruptions in the last 30m. thinking we should switch from price-optimized pools to capacity-optimized for the next 4h window and add a lightweight fallback ladder.
Phil: ugh. can you share which instance types are affected?
Anya: mostly a100-v4 and v100 mixes. 3 pools impacted: a) price-opt multi-zone b) reserved-mixed c) preemptible-only.
Kevin: capacity-opt tends to be more stable for bursty training. price-opt saves more $$ long term but is noisy. for latency-sensitive inferencing i'd avoid price-opt.
Sara: our SLOs for batch jobs are loose (24h), but serving lanes are 100ms tail. mixing is tricky. What's the suggested fallback ladder?
Anya: proposing ladder: 1) try capacity-optimized primary pool (same region) 2) if capacity under 70% success -> fall back to secondary region capacity-opt (eu-central-1) 3) burst to on-demand for critical serving lanes only 4) for non-critical batches, accept slower queue.
Phil: how about warm buffer? keep 5 nodes warm in eu-west-1 (spot) and 2 on-demand hot spares?
Kevin: warm buffer helps coldstart but costs. run a quick calc: if 5 a100 hot spares ~= $X/hr vs expected reclaim downtime cost Y.
spot-bot: automatic alert — 2020-05-12 10:14Z: spot churn metric eu-west-1 a100-v4 crossed threshold (15%).
Sara: we should also change bidding strategy for the price-opt pool to include a min-bid floor to reduce flips. i.e. prefer slightly higher bids (90th percentile) to trade cost for stability.
Anya: agreed. also enable soft-eviction: when reclaim predicted, drain new tasks and mark nodes as spillable.
Phil: can we show a sample k8s/placer config for mixed pools? quick snippet:
```
placement:
  - name: capacity-primary
    type: spot
    strategy: capacity_optimized
    zones: [eu-west-1a, eu-west-1b]
    min_bid_pct: 85
  - name: price-follower
    type: spot
    strategy: price_optimized
    max_price_pct: 70
  - name: on_demand_fallback
    type: on_demand
    reserved: 2
warm_buffer:
  capacity_primary: 5
  on_demand_spares: 2
fallback_policy: ladder
```
Kevin: nice. add node labels so scheduler can prefer capacity-primary for jobs with <1s coldstart budget.
Sara: also add telemetry tags: spot_pool, strategy, bid_pct — helps analyze which pools save vs break.
Anya: I'll roll a short experiment: 4h window, capacity-opt primary + min-bid floor 85%, warm buffer 3 (reduce cost) and on-demand spares 1. target: cut interruption rate under 5% and keep cost increase <10%. will report back.
Phil: set alert for reclaimed >5% or provisioning latency >90th pct for serving routes.
spot-bot: note: scheduled policy change queued — apply window at 2020-05-12T11:00Z. :gear:
Kevin: one more thing — network egress constraints: if we failover region, watch cross-region egress and KMS latency for private deployments. add a circuit-breaker to avoid cascading fallbacks.
Anya: noted. I'll include egress/cost guardrails. thanks all :thumbsup:
Sara: FYI — toggled tracing on the experiment group so we can associate regressions to model runs.
Phil: lmk if you need help with the rollout script, I can pair for 30m.
Anya: thanks — pairing would help. i'll DM availability.
